findings.title: Fallback copy creates output with default permissions and applies source mode only after the full write
findings.message: In the copy fallback the output file is created with the default umask-derived mode (typically 0644). The source's real mode is applied only at the end, after the whole archive has been copied and fsynced. For the whole copy, a private SDK archive may be readable by other local users. A crash before fchmod leaves a partial file with the wrong permissions. The hardlink path preserves the source mode, so the two paths behave differently.
findings.suggestion: Create the file with the intended mode from the start, for example `fd = os.open(output, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, source.stat().st_mode & 0o777)` and wrap it with `os.fdopen(fd, 'wb')`. Alternatively, restrict the mode to 0o600 on creation and widen it only after the copy completes. Note that the creation mode is still filtered by the umask.
